quotes.text: tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin.

rationale: The packet names the dataset (MIMIC-IV), version 2.2, snapshot date (January 2023), platform (PhysioNet) and a task-to-source-record route. This meets all anchor parts for 2. The MIMIC-IV statement sits uneasily with the public datasets named elsewhere in S1 (LUMIERE, BRACS and others); this is an internal S1 inconsistency, noted but not scored down.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
the source institution's review board determined that the study qualified for a waiver of consent.
BRACS | Dataset | Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International; used for non-commercial research evaluation with citation.

rationale: Origin and collection (routine-care hospital database, 2008-2019), terms (DUA; per-asset licences in Table 11) and consent status (IRB waiver) are all stated. The account of the data origin is inconsistent between the hospital-database statements and the public-dataset licence table; noted only.

searched: S1 (paper and appendix, including Table 4 text and Appendix C), S2 none, S3 none, S4 (a comment in agent_eval/notes.py describes a demographic comparison, but code comments never count as reporting under G1a), S5 none. No S1-S3 comparison to a target population and no descriptive patient-feature statistics or sampling design were found.

quotes.text: Safety testing identifies unsafe outputs like contraindicated medications; bias testing compares accuracy across different patient demographics.

rationale: S1 reports both an unsafe-output test and a bias test as built into the benchmark. No results of either test appear elsewhere in the packet; the score reflects the stated presence of both.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: Developer-side controls are present (private held-out split, canary string, no web access during runs). No measured overlap or contamination check is reported, so the anchor for 2 is not met.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: S1 states the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time and names the mechanism (no network path from the sandbox; labels not published in the repository).

searched: S1 (no statement that data, software image or evaluator are pinned or frozen; only citation access dates), S2 none, S3 none, S4 (a comment in notes.py claims the environment is frozen, but code comments do not count under G1a), S5 none. Nothing pinned is reported on S1-S3.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for every task and the result (all 120 graded correct) is reported.

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged, so out-of-scope modifications are detected and counted as failures.

rationale: Tasks change environment state (Analysis Operators create derived study state), so NA does not apply. The grader checks unchanged as well as changed state, which meets the anchor for 2.

quotes.text: Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: An empirical random-agent rate (2.5%) and a no-action rate (0.0%) are reported across all tasks.

quotes.text: Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: Do-nothing and random-agent scores are reported for all 120 tasks.

quotes.text: Grader validation tested 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, yielding 1% false acceptance and 2% false rejection rates.
We validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3%

rationale: The benchmark's own validation with error figures is reported (150 injected outcomes with 1%/2% error; separately 200 physician-labelled outputs with 94% agreement). The two validations differ in design and figures; both meet the anchor for 2.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens

rationale: S1 states seeds and a repeated-run policy (five runs, means reported). The reported score stands at 2. A code comment states temperature 0 where S1 states 0.7, so a candidate contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: Statistical testing of the two top-performing models employed paired permutation testing with p = 0.02.

rationale: A paired permutation test (p = 0.02) for the top-model comparison and 95% bootstrap CIs on model scores are reported.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7
the reported scores are means over the five independent runs.

contradiction_quotes.text: with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens

rationale: All three elements are on S1: five runs per task, seeds and temperature, and independence of runs. A code comment gives temperature 0 against S1's 0.7, flagged as a candidate contradiction.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task; where several tasks share a patient
we resample patients instead to account for clustering.

rationale: 95% bootstrap CIs, the resampling unit (task) and patient clustering handling (resample patients) are all stated.

quotes.text: Figure 7 shows that only 3 of 10 runs complete this functional sequence.
Even with identical inputs, the final axial, coronal, and sagittal views differ markedly across runs.

rationale: Appendix G.5 reports agreement of action sequences across 10 identical reruns (3 of 10 complete the sequence) and divergence of final viewer state across the same runs. No pass^k metric is given.

quotes.text: the temperature was set to 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens

rationale: S1 gives family names with release-year citations only (no snapshot IDs); the S4 comment lists different models (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022), so under the A4 exception identifiers count as absent. Decoding temperature is on S1 (0.7), but the S4 comment says 0, flagged. A harness release appears only in a code comment, so element (iii) is absent.

quotes.text: Each tool is defined by a JSON schema listing its name, arguments and argument types.
The documentation states for every tool whether it only reads or also writes state
describes what each tool returns, including the error message returned for invalid arguments.
These tool descriptions are included in the agent prompt.

rationale: JSON schemas, read/write documentation per tool and return and error semantics are all stated. S1 states the descriptions are included in the agent prompt, so the read/write property reaches the agent-visible surface (no S5 chunk is in the packet to confirm).

quotes.text: The agent interacts with a simulated hospital environment.

rationale: No tests or conformance checks of the tools are reported. S1 discloses that the environment is simulated, but gives no detail on which tools are simulated or stubbed, and no S5 chunk is present to show the disclosure reaches the agent. S5 reach cannot be told.

The agent interacts with a simulated hospital environment.
so out-of-scope modifications are detected and counted as failures.

rationale: Some actions change state, so NA does not apply. S1 identifies state-creating operations, says the environment is simulated, and says out-of-scope modifications are scored as failures. No S5 chunk shows whether the simulated/sandboxed status reaches the agent prompt, so S5 reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: Grading operates on the final environment state.
Grader validation tested 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, yielding 1% false acceptance and 2% false rejection rates.

rationale: The grader input is the final environment state, so a rationale for a non-state grader is not needed (element ii counted as satisfied). Validation on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates is reported.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: Leakage controls (no web access, restricted retrieval), a private held-out split kept off public surfaces and a canary string on released tasks are all stated.

Pathology CAMELYON17 [ 57 , 71 ] Lymph-node whole-slide image 550 Tumor presence and largest metastasis category

rationale: Results are given per task family, and Table 4 text gives case counts per module (e.g. 550 for CAMELYON17), though the counts are only partly visible and are not stated alongside each result. No results per patient subgroup are reported; the bias-test sentence states a comparison but no subgroup figures. No statement that demographic fields are absent.
